title: IAM access guidelines: hosted/dedicated/private
body:
Purpose:
This document defines recommended IAM role groupings, environment-specific access rules, short policy templates, audit log schema, SIEM export mappings, and a high-level evidence automation flow for periodic compliance checks. It focuses on differences between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and provides concrete guidance for SRE, platform, product, and security reviewers.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to: control plane, model serving control plane APIs, console, metrics and logs, and SIEM exports.
- Not in scope: customer-managed on-prem application code (except where Redwood agent/service accounts run).
- Assumes SSO/SCIM provisioning into group names described below; service accounts use short-lived tokens where possible.

High-level recommendations (quick):
- Principle: least privilege + environment scoping + auditable breakglass.
- Use environment-tagged roles (env=hosted|dedicated|private) rather than global admin roles.
- All admin-level changes require a Jira change ticket ID and must be accompanied by evidence bundle (snapshot + signed manifest).
- Breakglass access requires 2-step escalation and is fully logged and time-limited.

Role matrix (conceptual):
- Platform-Viewer-{env}: read-only for control plane metadata, config, dashboards. No access to secrets or raw request logs.
- Platform-Operator-{env}: manage deployment lifecycle, restart nodes, scale pools. No secret material access.
- Platform-Admin-{env}: full control-plane modify rights, incl. model rollout policies and routing. Requires manager approval.
- Security-Observer-{env}: read access to audit logs, SIEM exports, config drift reports.
- Customer-View (hosted): tenant-scoped view of usage, tokens, and model versions for that customer only.
- Customer-Admin (hosted/dedicated): tenant-scoped config + API key management for customer-owned resources. Not applicable in private unless customer configures.
- ServiceAccount:inference-runner-{env}: runtime-only identity used by inference nodes; scoped to model execution and metrics emission.
- ServiceAccount:siem-exporter: write-only to log sink; no console privileges.

Environment-specific rules and examples:
- Hosted:
  - Tenant data separation enforced via tenant_id resource tags.
  - Customer-Admin roles limited to org:tenant/{tenant_id} resources.
  - Internal Platform-Admin-hosted must use Just-In-Time (JIT) for emergency ops; all JIT sessions logged with approval ticket and TTL <= 1 hour.
  - No Platform-Admin-hosted account should have persistent direct DB credentials; use ephemeral credentials.

- Dedicated:
  - Dedicated clusters map to customer projects. Platform Operators can perform infra ops but must not access raw customer request payloads.
  - Customer has ability to request elevated role for deployment; elevation must produce evidence bundle and be scoped to a timeframe.
  - SIEM exporter configured per-dedicated-instance; security team can read but must request access if deeper than aggregate metrics.

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Customer-managed environment: Redwood provides control-plane package. Redwood staff access limited by contract and requires customer-scheduled window and access key with rotation.
  - Recommend using a remote attestation / signed manifest mechanism for evidence rather than Redwood-central logs.
  - Breakglass: local operator/hosted support to follow customer-specific escalation and record audit triplets (actor, reason, ticket).

Policy templates (short, pseudo-policy for RBAC v2 catalog):
- Minimal deployment policy (text pseudo-format):
  - name: deploy-model-limited
    allow: ["model.deploy", "model.version:list"]
    resources: ["org:{org_id}/project:{proj_id}/model:{model_id}"]
    constraints: { environment: ["dedicated","hosted"] }
    conditions: { requester_type: ["service_account","user"], require_ticket: true }

- Read-only console policy:
  - name: console-read-only
    allow: ["console.view","metrics.read","auditlog.search"]
    deny: ["secret.read","keymaterial.export"]
    resources: ["org:{org_id}/*"]

- Breakglass temporary elevation (workflow metadata):
  - name: breakglass-jit
    allow: ["*"]
    ttl_seconds: 3600
    require: ["ticket_id","manager_approval","mfa_assertion"]
    audit: ["snapshot_before","snapshot_after","executing_actor"]

Audit log schema (canonical fields - required):
- event_timestamp: ISO8601 string (consumer maps to @timestamp)
- event_id: UUID
- actor_id: SSO id or service-account id
- actor_type: user|service_account|api_key
- actor_source: console|api|admin-jit|agent
- action: canonical action name (model.deploy, route.update, key.rotate, auth.fail, token.issue, siem.export)
- resource_type: e.g., model, route, cluster, secret, api_key
- resource_id: resource identifier (tenant-scoped when applicable)
- outcome: success|failure|partial
- client_ip: IP address if known
- user_agent: optional
- request_id: correlated request id for tracing
- prev_state_hash: short hash of previous config snapshot (optional but preferred)
- change_summary: single-line human summary of change
- evidence_refs: list of evidence object ids (signed manifest, snapshot path)

SIEM export mapping & guidance:
- Recommended index/naming: redwood-audit-<env>-YYYY.MM.DD (e.g. redwood-audit-hosted-2026.03.05)
- Elastic mapping suggestions:
  - event_timestamp -> @timestamp
  - actor_id -> user.id
  - actor_type -> user.type
  - action -> event.action
  - resource_type -> object.type
  - resource_id -> object.id
  - outcome -> event.outcome
  - request_id -> trace.id
  - client_ip -> source.ip
  - evidence_refs -> files.evidence_ids
- CEF/LEEF forwarding: include a compact mapping with event_id and minimal actor/resource info; keep full JSON in primary sink.
- Retention/forwarding notes: audit logs must be immutable in primary bucket for at least 365 days for enterprise customers; export to SIEM (Splunk/Elastic/Datadog) for 90-day interactive retention.

Evidence automation (operational workflow):
1) Daily snapshot job: capture RBAC assignments, active service accounts, recent JIT sessions, and a checksum of current role-policy files. Store in evidence-bucket:/snapshots/<env>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/manifest.json (signed by key-management service).
2) On-change hook: when a policy or role mapping changes, trigger evidence builder that attaches the Jira ticket, PR link, approvers, and the diff between snapshots.
3) Audit bundle creation: packaged zip with logs (time-window limited), manifest, snapshot, and a signed hash. Upload to long-term evidence store with object metadata containing ticket_id.
4) Reviewer flow: compliance reviewer can request an evidence bundle via UI or Jira subtask and an automated pre-built bundle is returned with signed tamper-evidence.

Operational playbooks and notes:
- Onboarding new admin group: require SCIM group name, owner email, least-privilege justification, and a retention plan. Add to nightly snapshot watchlist.
- Offboarding: immediately remove from SCIM and trigger evidence snapshot. If offboarding affects private deployments, notify customer ops channel.
- Emergency procedure (e.g., customer data exfil suspicion): escalate to SOC, preserve all audit logs, create forensics branch with immutable copies, do not rotate keys until a forensics snapshot is taken (documented).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we standardize TTL for all JIT sessions to 3600s or allow per-role overrides? (Security prefers 3600, Platform prefers per-role).
- How to surface per-tenant RBAC exports for hosted customers who request their full access report? API or scheduled delivery?

Next steps / owners:
- Lina: prototype the daily snapshot + signed manifest automation (Jira: JIRA-SEC-1301).
- Marcus: map current audit logs to recommended fields and provide sample ingest pipeline (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/598).
- Evelyn (owner): align contract language for private deployments regarding breakglass and evidence collection.

References and links:
- See linked artifacts at top for design doc and PR.
- Quick checklist for reviewers: 1) verify ticket_id on admin changes, 2) ensure evidence_refs present in audit events, 3) validate snapshot signature for >90 days.
